person.bibl: Ariav, Talia (2002). ‘Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita: An Independent Poet of the Kaveri Delta, or: The Forgotten Model of Genealogical Authorship’. In The Indian Economic and Social History Review 59(3): 273–298.
person.note: Another of his teachers is Veṅkaṭeśvara Makhin. See Talia, Ariav. "Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita: An Independent Poet of the Kaveri Delta, or: The Forgotten Model of Genealogical Authorship". The Indian Economic and Social History Review 59(3) (2022): 273–298: p. 275.

He had four brothers. His elder brother was Accān. His youngest brother was Atirātra Yajvan. His immediate younger brother was Appayya Dīkṣita (often refered to as Appayya III). See Talia, Ariav. "Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita: An Independent Poet of the Kaveri Delta, or: The Forgotten Model of Genealogical Authorship". The Indian Economic and Social History Review 59(3) (2022): 273–298.
His father was Nārāyaṇādhvariṇ. His grandfather was Accān Dīkṣita.
